ted banning.name: Ted Banning
ted banning.origin: Ted Banning was an American counter-espionage agent after the end of World War II. He was sent to Buenos Aires to compile a list of escaped Nazi war criminals in 1946. Once he had completed his list he was on his way back to Washington, D.C. when he was captured by agents working for a former Nazi named Rex. Ted's disappearance led to the United States government to send Miss America on a mission to rescue Ted and recover the list of escaped Nazis. While in the clutches of Rex Herr, Ted was shackled in the former Nazi's hideout while he sought to obtain a sun-ray formula, gloating that he would use the ray to take over the world. However, Herr obtained a phony copy of the formula and captured Miss America making her prisoner along with Ted. When demanding the location of the formula, Herr threatened to torture Ted. Miss America then tricked Rex to seek out her alter-ego Madeline Joyce, hoping the wild goose chase would allow the two of them to escape. However, Miss America failed to free them and when Rex return he had his men tie the two up to a mining cart strapped with TNT and sent them speeding down a mine shaft to their doom. Miss America freed herself from their bonds and pulled Ted to safety, but the resulting blast caused a minor cave in trapping them in the mine. The pair then dug their way out, and Miss America carried the exhausted Ted to safety while she went after Rex Herr and the formula. Eventually Ted recovered enough to gather a number of American counter-espionage agents and followed a telegram sent by Miss America to the home of former Nazi general Eric Kesselwolfe, Rex's rival for the formula. They arrived and slaughtered Herr and Kesselwolfe's men in a gun battle and Rex and Kesselwolfe were soon captured and the sun-ray formula recovered. Ted's subsequent activities are unknown.
weapons: Ted carries a government issue firearm.

ted carter.name: Ted Carter
ted carter.origin: Ted Carter was a scientist who was very much in love with the beautiful actress Wendy Grey, to whom he continued to give her expensive gifts. When one day Wendy asked him for $10,000 to operate on her mother, even though that amount was all of her savings, he granted it by writing her a check. Realizing shortly after that he had forgotten to put the date on the check, he returned to Wendy's house and there he listened through the door that she was in the company of a man and they were making fun of him after he had given him the money with which they intended to gamble at roulette. Wanting revenge, Ted returned to the laboratory and created a special cream there, then called Wendy telling her that the cream he had created especially for her would prevent the signs of aging from appearing. Wendy excitedly did it, and as she did it she thought how envious Sherry Lamour and Hedy Turner, her beauty rivals, would be when they began to wrinkle as she grew older. Shortly after spreading the cream all over her body, Wendy began to feel pain and then completely transformed into a statue of solid basalt, so Ted got her revenge without however affecting Wendy's beauty.

ted castle.name: Ted Castle
ted castle.origin: Little information is known about Ted Castle. He was married to Alyssa Moy who was Reed Richards' ex-girlfriend. Years after, he and Alyssa created a world for the replacement of the original one for their theory that Earth will soon be doomed and there is no solution to stop it. This world is called Nu-World. However, Ted is aware that Alyssa still loves Reed. Ted is as intelligent as his wife and very rich, but although he is wealthy, his wealth is still not enough to supply the needs for their project Nu-World. Like his wife and Reed, CAP is also programmed not to hurt him. Ted did not have the good intentions that he outwardly displayed, fooling even his wife into believing him to be a humanitarian. Secretly, Nu-World was for the rich and powerful. Ted and the other benefactors planned to leave almost everyone else on Earth behind to die so they could recreate the world in their image. His plan was foiled after Alyssa told this to the Fantastic Four and they used Nu-World as a location for six billion refugees from a dying future. Upon the arrival of the New Defenders, Ted had a robot army prepared to take them into custody for their removal. So they could not get any help, he destroyed the portal off the planet. He planned to take the remaining heroes to Nu-Moon and then figure out a way to remove all the people from his world. When they refused to cooperate, Ted ordered his robots to detach the core of Nu-World, which would turn the planet into an uninhabitable world of ice. With the help of Alyssa Moy, Hulk Jr. remotely activated the self-destruct mechanism of Nu-Moon, thus leaving Ted no choice but to call of his robots and leave the world habitable for his sake. Ted swore that he would find a way to remove them from his planet. The solution came to him in a dream when a mysterious woman from that dying Earth claimed she wanted her children back. The woman was Mother Earth herself, Gaea, driven insane by the lack of life on her planet. Ted sided with her because they had the same goal: get the people off Nu-Earth. Gaea and her Hysteries were eventually defeated and it would seem that Ted and Alyssa became reconnected when they teamed up to try and stop Ego the Living Planet from destroying Nu-World. thumb|left After some time, the sun collapsed in on itself, turning into a black hole and accelerating time rapidly. In this time, the people of Nu-World lost their will to live and war and chaos ensued. Lightwave and Alex Ultron of the New Defenders took over control of the planet. Ted and Alyssa became outlaws stuck on the planet because the portal to escape was broken. Ted had hoped to find Reed Richards, but instead got his genius daughter Valeria. She provided Ted with a power source capable of fixing the portal and steering Nu-World away from the black hole. He remained behind with his creation.

Like his wife and Reed, CAP is also programmed not to hurt him. Ted did not have the good intentions that he outwardly displayed, fooling even his wife into believing him to be a humanitarian. Secretly, Nu-World was for the rich and powerful. Ted and the other benefactors planned to leave almost everyone else on Earth behind to die so they could recreate the world in their image. His plan was foiled after Alyssa told this to the Fantastic Four and they used Nu-World as a location for six billion refugees from a dying future. Upon the arrival of the New Defenders, Ted had a robot army prepared to take them into custody for their removal. So they could not get any help, he destroyed the portal off the planet. He planned to take the remaining heroes to Nu-Moon and then figure out a way to remove all the people from his world. When they refused to cooperate, Ted ordered his robots to detach the core of Nu-World, which would turn the planet into an uninhabitable world of ice. With the help of Alyssa Moy, Hulk Jr. remotely activated the self-destruct mechanism of Nu-Moon, thus leaving Ted no choice but to call of his robots and leave the world habitable for his sake. Ted swore that he would find a way to remove them from his planet. The solution came to him in a dream when a mysterious woman from that dying Earth claimed she wanted her children back. The woman was Mother Earth herself, Gaea, driven insane by the lack of life on her planet. Ted sided with her because they had the same goal: get the people off Nu-Earth. Gaea and her Hysteries were eventually defeated and it would seem that Ted and Alyssa became reconnected when they teamed up to try and stop Ego the Living Planet from destroying Nu-World. thumb|left After some time, the sun collapsed in on itself, turning into a black hole and accelerating time rapidly. In this time, the people of Nu-World lost their will to live and war and chaos ensued. Lightwave and Alex Ultron of the New Defenders took over control of the planet. Ted and Alyssa became outlaws stuck on the planet because the portal to escape was broken. Ted had hoped to find Reed Richards, but instead got his genius daughter Valeria. She provided Ted with a power source capable of fixing the portal and steering Nu-World away from the black hole. He remained behind with his creation.

ted chambers.name: Ted Chambers

During the flight home to Los Angeles he swapped the baggage with Peter Parker who was traveling to join his wife in Hollywood. When he opened the suitcase, Ted discovered the costume of Spider-Man and decided to wear it before jumping from the window of the building to commit suicide but accidentally his fall was dampened by a large tent and then ruined on a thief who was robbing a passerby. The passerby was convinced that was really a hero who had saved him and Ted decided to continue the fiction claiming to be Spider-Man West. After various adventures Ted was convinced to not be a true hero and he decided to dispose of the suit but just then acted as a hero by helping to save several people from a fire.

ted emmett.name: Ted Emmett
ted emmett.origin: Ted Emmett was the father of Tally Emmett and the longtime rival of Mr. Powers. The two men had once been business partners, but during a period of financial hardship Powers sold his shares to Ted shortly before a sudden economic boom transformed Emmett into a wealthy man while the Powers family continued to struggle financially. The incident created lasting bitterness between the two families. After Tally and Kip Powers ran away together into the swamps near Citrusville, Ted joined the search party looking for them. When the Emmetts and Powerses encountered one another in the swamp, old hostilities quickly resurfaced. As Tally became trapped in quicksand, Ted desperately attempted to save her. Unable to reach her safely, he begged Powers to hold him by the ankles so he could extend himself farther into the mire. Powers refused, effectively sealing Tally’s fate as she drowned before her father's eyes. Following Tally’s death and Kip’s subsequent suicide, Ted and Powers continued fighting one another despite the tragedy that had destroyed both families.

ted larkin.name: Ted Larkin

It eventually found its way into the computers of the United States Air Force. From there, it got downloaded into Box, who was receiving information from the USAF. The virus took over the Box robot and flew back to the Air Force base in an attempt to transfer the only units it could locate; nuclear missiles. Madison was able to finally phase out and destroy the robot. The virus apparently still existed in the USAF database as when a new piece of automated targetting hardware was interfaced to the computer system, the computer "transferred" some missile units to Ted Larkin personally.

ted of the five tunnels.name: Ted of the Five Tunnels
ted of the five tunnels.origin: Ted of the Five Tunnels was a member of a collective of Moloids who lived beneath the Keewazi Reservation in Oklahoma. When the Keewazi entered into an agreement with Roxxon to let them drill their land, the perforation disturbed the maze of subterranean passages where Ted's collective lived. The Moloids attacked the surface in reataliation, but Keewazi leader Wyatt Wingfoot managed to defuse the situation. After making amends, the Keewazi welcomed the Moloids into their tribe. The Moloids coexisted in the surface for a week until the Mole Man became aware of their mingling with the Keewazi and threatened them to return underground. In response, Wyatt signalled the Fantastic Four, but the call was only heeded by the Human Torch and his partner Sky. A day after issuing the warning, the Mole Man attacked Silver Rock Springs with a group of dinosaurs. A fight broke out until Sky used her powers to explain to the Mole Man's dinosaurs that their master was in the wrong, putting an abrupt end to his intrusion.

ted sparks.name: Ted Sparks
ted sparks.origin: thumb|left|176px|Ted Sparks Ted Sparks was an accomplished horror writer in the 1940s. He was eccentric and surrounded his Greenwich Village apartment with various horror props, intended to inspire his writing. He was engaged to marry a woman named Peggy. One day in 1948, Sparks was seemingly ignored by Peggy, after he asked her to mend his socks. Friends with the Human Torch and Toro, Sparks expressed his frustrations with Peggy. He vowed to write a horror story based on a jilted lover, on the assumption that Peggy was going to leave him. The Torch and Toro left him to write his story while they went to find out what was wrong with Peggy. Sparks fell asleep at his typewriter, and dreamed that his evil self -- called Mephisto -- was loose on the world and went out to propose to various women. Those who turned him down, he killed, clashing with the Human Torch and Toro. However, when the heroes finally caught up with him, he was singed by a fireball... Only to wake up finding it was all a dream and his sleeve caught fire on an overturned candle. The flame was put out by the arriving Peggy who explained that she was busy the past few days because she was knitting him new socks. With the situation sorted out, Sparks thanked the Torch and Toro for straightening things out for him and Peggy.

teela coldassian.name: Teela Coldassian
teela coldassian.origin: Princess Teela was born to a life of privilege on the Krook homeworld, but like all Krook she had to endure the trials to become an adult and a full member of Krook society. When the Krook people threw the Omega Confederation off of their world they hired a group of mercenaries to help defend the mines the Confederation had built. The Omega Confederation hired the Deadpool Corps to take back the world for them. Teela was the first Krook to encounter the Corps right after they wiped out a patrol of mercenaries, except for one to use in there negotiations with the king. Teela saw this and ran to tell her people but was forced to fight Lady Deadpool and eventually lost the fight. Later the Deadpool Corps turned on their employers and set about modernizing the world. Eventually there was a split between the Krook people which lead to a small civil war, with one faction following the tradition-minded King while another declared progressive Teela the new Queen. This also split the Deadpool Corps, with Lady Deadpool, Kidpool, and Dogpool siding with the King and Deadpool and Headpool siding with Teela. This later turned out to be an elaborate ruse when the Deadpool Corps robbed the bank in the Krook capital and escaped the planet with all of the Krook's gold. Lady Deadpool and Teela fought one last time with Lady Deadpool winning a second time. Although the Deadpool Corps got away, Teela and her father reconciled and vowed to allow the Krook to follow the traditional and the progressive paths as they chose. Teela also revealed she never trusted Deadpool, and had replaced all the gold in the vaults with painted lead.

fields.history: Like other Stygian soldiers, Tefnet had been sent by the overlords of Khemi to act as guards on Stygian merchant vessels as protection against the Black Corsairs. The ship guarded by Tefnet and others transported a young albino girl (later revealed to be a denizen from the fabled Mountains of Madness). Despite Tefnet's belief the Black Corsairs would never approach the Stygian vessels now they knew they were armed, he was the first victim of the ship's boarding by Bêlit's Black Corsairs.
fields.trivia: Tefnet was presumably named after Tefnut, one of the Ennead (or Heliopolitan gods) of Egypt.

tefral.name: Tefral
tefral.origin: ===Celestial War=== Predating the Multiverse by many times over, Tefral was one of the Celestials from the First Cosmos, the first-ever universe. They rebelled against their creator, the First Firmament, and the Aspirants, shattering the First Cosmos into the Second Cosmos, the first-ever Multiverse. This began the multiversal cycles. The Celestials created and/or appointed many beings to serve them, including but not limited to the Exterminators, Cal-Horra, and the Omegas. Each time the Multiverse ended, the Celestials passed on to the next incarnation of the Multiverse. At some point, the Celestials also began to assign Kings in Black. Although split across the Multiverse, the Celestials' counterparts are interconnected aspects of themselves and not separate beings. Thus, the Tefral of Earth-616 is one aspect of the true Tefral. ===Earth-616=== A Celestial that specializes in surveying the landscape. He is one of the few Celestials that actually explored the planet during the First Host. ===Multiverse=== The Celestials exist across the Multiverse simultaneously. A Celestial's alternate reality selves are actually aspects of the same being. Despite this, their alternate aspects may have very different histories from the ones in the mainstream Marvel Universe. ====Earth-9997==== Tefral is a member of the Celestial race. Having long since evolved past physical bodies, the Celestials reproduced by impregnating a planet with their essence, which in time would gestate into an infant Celestial. To protect the growing fetus, they would genetically modify the people of said world, greatly enhancing their evolutionary potential and imbuing them with a certain level of aggressiveness. One of these impregnated planets was Earth. After the populace of Earth fully mutated prematurely, Tefral and other Celestials travelled to the world to purge it of all life before they could threaten the infant Celestial. They were met with opposition from Black Bolt on the Moon, Tefral and the Celestials killed Black Bolt and then set their sights on Earth. On Earth, they were opposed by Namor and an army of sea creatures, Tony Stark in a giant robotic factor and an army of Iron Men robots, and an army of Asgardians led by Loki. This bought the Earth precious moments for the arrival of "Galactus" (actually Franklin Richards) who was called to Earth by Black Bolt before his death. Galactus was able to fight off the Celestials, and Tefral was one of the Celestials felled in the battle. ====Earth-20208==== thumb|none When Earth-20208 was pruned from the timestream by Immortus and the reality was dying from entropy, Reed Richards killed Celestials, including Tefral, and drank their their blood so he could use their power to save the timeline. ====Earth-90251==== thumb|none Tefral and all of the Celestials were killed by Doctor Doom in a battle that lasted 407 years, after Doom gained the power of the Beyonder and the Infinity Gauntlet. ====Earth-16524==== thumb|none ====Earth-TRN909==== thumb|none Tefral was killed alongside the universe's galactic empires, Galactus, and the other Celestials by Annihilus during his universal conquest. ====Earth-TRN1539==== left|thumb Tefral was among the Celestials that judged Woodgod for having destroyed his village with his powers.

tegnar.name: Tegnar
tegnar.origin: Tegnar was one of the Balkatars of the Cat People, a title the Sorcerers Guild gave to the one who would answer the Sorcerers call. When Helene and Flavius, the first members of the Cat People created by Ebrok, tried to protect themselves from the wrath of the Sorcerers Guild, they summoned Balkatar. He was unable to help them, still a thrall of the Sorcerers Guild, even though he wanted to. After the Sorcerers Guild was defeated by the first Tigra, no longer having to answer to the Sorcerers' orders, Helene and Flavius ​​arranged for Balkatar and Tigra to mate, thus giving birth to the second generation of Cat People.

tehru.name: Tehru
tehru.origin: Tehru was a native of India who supported the Japanese against the Americans during World War II. He was sent by Imperial Japanese officials to raid the American consulate in India for documents that might have been useful for the war effort. During this raid, the spies were opposed by the Young Allies, whom they outnumbered and captured, with the exception of Toro, who escaped and followed the kidnappers. Tehru tried to use his magics to get the natives of Burma to support the Japanese in their struggles against the Americans, by making it look like their gods supported the Japanese. Toro destroyed this illusion and made himself appear as a god through the use of his powers, persuading the villagers to support the Americans. The boys were again captured as a unit of Japanese soldiers showed up at about this same time. Tehru was to be executed for his failure, but the commanding officer decided to give him one more chance to redeem himself. This time, he plotted to use mirrors to make it appear as if the Japanese soldiers were attacking from a different locations than they actually were. This plan also failed due to the interference of the Young Allies, and the Japanese were easily defeated. Tehru attempted to escape once he saw this, but fell into a pit trap and was killed.
abilities: Tehru was a skilled illusionist, able to use smoke and mirrors for a variety of effects, including the appearance of teleportation and of making others appear to be in different locations than they actually were.

teju.name: Teju
teju.origin: Teju was a Reptoid selected by the Prime Mover to be one of six pawns who would serve him in his contest against the Grandmaster for ownership of Earth. Each squad was divided into three teams of two, and Teju was partnered with the Fomalhauti Dumog. After the Grandmaster's pawns won the first round, Teju and Dumog were teleported to an arena world that was full of volcanic eruptions and oppressive heat where their opponents were the Sub-Mariner and Daredevil. Teju struck first, attacking the Sub-Mariner while Dumog battled Daredevil. Weakened by the burning heat, the Sub-Mariner was unable to harm Teju because of the Reptoid's natural armor, and Namor's situation became even more dire after a slash from Teju's tail destroyed his costume's moisture-recycling system. Once Dumog had killed Daredevil, Teju and the Sub-Mariner rushed each other but the Sub-Mariner was already too weak to strike more than one blow before, suffocating, he fell to the ground. Taking advantage of his helpless foe, Teju used his tail to beat the Sub-Mariner into a pulp, killing him and thereby winning the second round for the Prime Mover. The Grandmaster later resurrected the two heroes after his pawns won the third round, defeating the Prime Mover. One of the Prime Mover's other pawns, the cyborg Korvac, used power he had synthesized by analyzing the Grandmaster's energies to return to his native thirty-first century future where he planned to create his own empire. Deciding that his empire needed a loyal home guard, Korvac teleported the three other surviving pawns (Teju, Dumog and the Grund known as Grott the Manslayer) to his wonderworld where he recruited them, along with the Achernonian Brahl and the Procyonite Tork, to serve him as a team known as the Minions of Menace. When the thunder god Thor from the past and the Guardians of the Galaxy became caught up in the villain's schemes and came to Korvac's world to stop him, the seven heroes were met by the five Minions. Once Thor and Starhawk went on to confront Korvac, the Minions and Guardians began battling. The Minions initially more than held their own, with Teju using his slashing tail effectively against Charlie-27, but things changed when the Guardians switched opponents and Major Astro used his psyche-blasts to strike Teju with his own tail, knocking him out. Once his scheme was thwarted, Korvac teleported away. With Korvac gone, the Minions mostly split up to pursue their own interests. Teju ended up a prisoner on Stockade, a planet from which it was supposedly impossible to escape. He was freed by Brahl, who was reuniting the Minions so that they could bring his master plan to fruition. Now calling themselves the Intimidators, Teju and the other four traveled to Mainframe's World where they began secretly draining energy from the living computer Mainframe so that they could use data that Korvac had encoded on a chip in order to resurrect him. However, they were discovered by a new team of heroes, later known as the Galactic Guardians, before the process was completed. After Teju was punched out by Hollywood, Grott and Tork struck back, but all of the Intimidators except for Brahl were then defeated when they were encased in ice by Martinex. Brahl was able to resurrect Korvac, but in a crazed state. This Korvac was defeated when Phoenix removed Korvac from that reality and transported him to another.

fields.notes: When this character first appeared in , he was identified only as a "scaly man-lizard." It wasn't until he next appeared in that it was revealed that his name was Teju and that he was a Reptoid. Technically, although various Official Handbook profiles state that Teju and Dumog were two of the unnamed aliens who served the Prime Mover, there has so far never been any in-story references that confirm that either of them had been pawns of the Prime Mover. However, the fact that Len Wein was a co-plotter on both those comics suggests that Teju and the man-lizard were always meant to be one and the same. Teju first appeared in a story set in Earth-616's Modern Age and has since appeared only in stories set in Earth-691's thirty-first century. There has so far been no in-story evidence indicating which reality and time period is his point of origin.

telegon.name: Telegon
telegon.origin: Telegon was an Eternal whose records had become lost from the Machine that is Earth. Like the other Eternals, he was created by the Celestials a million years ago, but unlike the others, he was seemingly inactive for the majority of that time. In the modern era, an unidentified mother lost her young son, Rexel. Blaming the "gods," the Eternals, for not answering her prayers to bring him back, she decided to steal one of theirs, Telegon. Although he was unaware of even his own name at first, she planned to use him in vengeance against the Eternals and telepathically linked their minds, treating him as her replacement son. When the other Eternals found him, Ikaris was dispatched to bring him back to Olympia. As the Killswitch, Telegon used his powers to defend himself, teleporting objects and people from space and time. After Telegon had summoned a Celestial hand, indirectly bypassing the first principle, Ikaris returned to Zuras to report that more drastic measures were necessary.

telephus.name: Telephus
telephus.origin: Telephus was the son of Heracles the father of Eurypylus and the warrior-King of Teuthrania, in southern Mysia. After Paris of Troy stole Helen of Sparta from King Menelaus, Menelaus and his armies crossed the Aegean Sea to attack Troy. When they reached Teuthrania, the Argives sacked it, thinking it was Troy. Telephus killed Thersander, son of of Polyneices, and was himself wounded by Achilles (who used his godly-crafted ashen spear. Telephus wound festered, and he retrieved Achilles at Scyros, during his wedding with King Lycomedes' daughter Deïdameia. Achilles scraped some rust from his spear into the wound who instantly healed. Telephus refused to join Achilles against Troy, but showed him the course to steer to reach it. Nine to ten years later, his son Eurypylus later led an army to Troy against the Argives, and was killed by Achilles' son Neoptolemus.

teleplex.name: Teleplex
teleplex.origin: Teleplex is a member of the team of super-heroes sponsored by the Irish government called the Kinsmen. They were considered Ireland's answer to the Avengers. The Kinsmen were sent to Cassidy Keep to collect Sean Cassidy in the early morning hours for a long overdue debriefing by officials of the Irish government. However, the team discovered that he was not home, but they were greeted by his daughter, Theresa, and the Seneschal, Eamon O'Donnell. The team were brusk in their conversations with Theresa, demanding to know where her father was to the point a fight broke out between her and the Kinsmen. Teleplex, who had remained in the helicopter with their government liaison, Mr. McFadden, monitored their situation inside Cassidy Keep. At some point Teleplex's remote viewing of the situation was interrupted until Highlander came flying through the air out of Cassidy Keep. Moments later the rest of the team also left the building as they were unable to defeat the young mutant. Soon the angry Irishwoman took the defeated team to Mr. McFadden and Teleplex, telling them to leave her and her father alone and call first before they ever return to Cassidy Keep. Then she destroyed their expensive high-tech helicopter and left to find their own way home. Teleplex's subsequent fate remains unrecorded at this time, including whether or not he retained his mutant abilities after the events of M-Day.

he could literally see anything from all sides. : Teleplex could also use project those images on electronic displays.
weaknesses: Cowardly as he left his handler in the helicopter before Siryn destroyed it.

ten for.name: Ten-For
ten for.origin: Ten-For was an Autocron who tricked Machine Man into bringing him to earth by sending a message through an unknowing human pawn that his ship was crashing into a star. Arriving on Earth, Ten-For tried to kill the human he'd used as a conduit but was stopped by Machine Man, but Ten-For paralysed him and left to begin plans for world domination. Ten-For went on a rampage but was confronted by a recovered Machine-Man. The pair were evenly matched and Ten-For planned to just wait it out for the arrival of the rest of the Autocron fleet To this end he surrendered to the army and tried to act like Machine Man had been the aggressor. Ten-For grew bored of the army and revealed his true plan and went on another rampage. Machine Man arrived and was able to take control of him and used him as a nuclear bomb against his own arriving fleet. Ten-For survived and was captured by the enigmatic alien, the Stranger, and was imprisoned in the Stranger's Laboratory World for the alien to study him. He remained there until freed by Overmind.

ten thirtifor.name: Ten-Thirtifor
ten thirtifor.origin: An Autocron “holocaust specialist”, Ten-Thirtifor developed independent thought, which qualified as rebellion in his society, for which he was banished to Earth during its brief stint as a penal planet. He was among the small number of alien convicts that U.S.Agent recruited to break Ronan the Accuser's quarantine of Earth, and was present during the Earth's super-heroes' invasion of one of the Ruul's watchtowers in deep space. Ten-Thirtifor remained on Earth after the Maximum Security event was over, attempting to summon an invasion fleet in the hopes of being reinstated. He was resisted by the Avengers Iron Man, Warbird, and the Vision, who managed to waylay him after a high-frequency sonic attack. Left unconscious by Warbird, he was soon after taken into custody by S.H.I.E.L.D.
abilities: Capable of firing energy blasts with his faceplate lifted
weaknesses: Weak to sonic weapons

tenebrous.name: Tenebrous
tenebrous.origin: Tenebrous of the Darkness Between emerged at the dawn of the universe along with the other Proemial Gods and he maintained the "Black," the living matter that binds the universe and makes it whole. Along with Aegis, Lady of All Sorrows and most of the other Proemial Gods, Tenebrous was corrupted by Diableri of Chaos. He was defeated by Galactus and imprisoned in the Kyln with Aegis. Eons later, Tenebrous and Aegis were freed by Annihilus' forces with the destruction of the Kyln. They captured the Fallen One, a former Herald of Galactus, though he was serving Thanos at the time. They then encountered Thanos, who convinced them to defeat Galactus along with the Silver Surfer and deliver them to Annihilus for experimentation. After the events of the Annihilation Wave, Tenebrous and Aegis returned to the Kyln, discovering the corpse of their fellow Proemial God, Antiphon the Overseer. Galactus and the Silver Surfer had escaped from containment; the Silver Surfer engaged both Tenebrous and Aegis in battle and managed to channel the energies of the nearby Crunch, the barrier that separates the universe from the Negative Zone. Overwhelmed by the Crunch's energies, Tenebrous and Aegis were both seemingly killed. However, he and Aegis both survived their encounter with the Surfer, as they reappeared with Galactus and the Celestials to oppose the forces of the Cancerverse at the Fault. While Aegis was killed in the war, Tenebrous survived. His current whereabouts and activities are unknown.

tenelle.name: Tenelle
tenelle.origin: Lady Tenelle was a member of Skrull nobility, known as "the most beautiful woman in the Skrull galaxy". She was an ally of the Super-Skrull (Kl'rt) and in love with him. Kl'rt convinced her to marry Ward Meachum, his human ally, in order to seal their political alliance with each other. Ward was at first eager to marry a purported beauty. However he was later lead to doubt that beautiful by Skrull standards would be the same for a human. He betrayed Kl'rt and lost his life in the process. Tenelle was left to mourn the loss of her betrothed and the disgrace of her beloved.
powers: Skrull Shape-Shifting

terdu.name: Terdu
terdu.origin: Terdu was a criminal sorcerer who was active during the 1940s. In the spring of 1945 his home was invaded by mob leader "Terrible Tom" Garrett who was on the run from Captain America and Bucky. Terdu offered Garrett the means to eliminate Captain America and Bucky once and for all. Using his magic cauldron, Terdu summoned criminals from the past: Captain Kidd, Jack the Ripper, Jesse & Frank James, Bluebeard, and Gyp-the-Blood to the present to assist in this plan. After capturing the heroes, the so-called Masters of Evil returned to Terdu's home with their captives. Terdu demanded that they be defeated fairly and demanded that his minions battle Captain America one-on-one. Cap managed to beat all the Masters, and Terdu, in a fit of rage, banished them back to their native time periods. Charging at Captain America, Terdu missed the hero, and fell into his own cauldron, which apparently killed him.
abilities: Terdu is a sorcerer of unspecified mystical talent.
weaknesses: It appeared that immersing Terdu in the waters of his own cauldron were lethal.

teresa shining path.name: Teresa (Shining Path)
teresa shining path.origin: Little is known of Teresa's past. She was a Peruvian mutant who at some point embraced radical Communism and was recruited into the Shining Path terrorist group by Inza Cuzco along with other mutants. Maria usually worked with her fellow mutant, Maria and a baseline-human terrorist named Carla. Teresa was present with Inza and Maria when the Shining Path freed its imprisoned leader, Ernesto Sanz. She later helped capture Cable when he attempted to infiltrate the Shining Path's camp. She escaped the police's raid on the camp with Maria and Carla, and regrouped with Sanz and Inza at a safehouse, from which Sanz sent the three women to destroy and important lumber plant, which they did. Following Cable's defeat of Inza and Sanz, Maria, Teresa, and Carla took to armed robbery and held up a bank. Cable confronted them again and the three women attacked. Cable killed Maria and Teresa in self-defense. Shortly thereafter, Carla was also killed in an act of police brutality by her interrogating officer.
weapons: In addition to her powers, Teresa carried a pistol, which she used to murder a hostage at the bank robbery.

teresa sue bottoms.origin: Terri Sue Bottoms was the short-lived girlfriend of Bobby Drake, also the mutant hero known as Iceman. At the time Bobby kept his double-identity a secret, even from Terri. teresa vasquez.name: Teresa Vasquez
teresa vasquez.origin: Little is known of Fer-de-Lance's background before she became a professional criminal. She first appeared alongside a group of fellow snake-themed costumed criminals, Copperhead, Puff Adder, and Black Racer, who were robbing a Las Vegas casino in the hopes of being recruited by the criminal gang the Serpent Society. However, they were soon opposed by Captain America (at that time known as The Captain) and his allies Falcon, Nomad and Demolition-Man, who apprehended them. As the criminals had hoped, however, the Serpent Society's leader Sidewinder teleported into their police cells and offered them membership, which they accepted. One of the original serpents, Diamondback attempted to befriend Fer-de-Lance on her arrival at the Serpent Citadel. Fer-de-Lance expressed a romantic interest in Sidewinder, but after informing her that Sidewinder was involved with her teammate Black Mamba, Diamondback offered to set Fer-de-Lance up with another teammate, Rattler. It transpired that the Society's new recruits were actually working for the terrorist Viper, who wanted to take over the group herself. As part of the coup, Fer-de-Lance attacked Diamondback, but Diamondback knocked Fer-de-Lance into an equipment bank, causing her to electrocute herself, and escaped. Fer-de-Lance remained with the Society after King Cobra took over as leader, and clashed with Captain America again, among other heroes. ===Corrupted by Mephisto=== Fer-de-Lance was among the members of the Serpent Society who were, under unknown circumstances, corrupted by the demon Mephisto. After going on a bloodthirsty rampage throughout the Serpent Solutions headquarters, Fer-de-Lance and her teammates were defeated by Nighthawk. The Serpent Society later escaped custody and resumed their murderous activity on the Brooklyn Bridge.

terhali.origin: Terhali was the daughter of the king of Melniboné, and of a she-Demon summoned from the mortal plane of Earth. She became the Green Empress of Melniboné, and a fearfull sorceress. She seemingly spawned a descendance, which included Elric, who himself would later become the sorcerer-king of Melniboné. Eventually, she fell against the combined spells of her magic user foes, who sealed her in a tomb in the capital city Yagala, which they projected into the Hyborian World, circled around with magical barriers, and brought rains and floods to drown the city and the tomb (said to be a treasure-trove of sorcerous lore), leaving only the highest towers of the city to remain above the waters known as the Sighing Lake, in Eastern Koth. ...

terra x.species: Metamutant ( and Terrax were combined in a Marvel versus DC crossover)
terra x.origin: Terra-X was briefly mentioned as being a former member of the Mutant Titans, who had left the Titans and was the metamutant daughter of Dare the Terminator. Terra-X first appeared as a member of the X-Patrol who had joined the team after the fight against Doctor Doomsday, but soon betrayed them to X-Stroke the Eliminator. She even delivered Ferro Man to X-Stroke herself, but the X-Patrol broke free of X-Stroke. Shatterstarfire, who was not present on this mission, noticed Terra-X escaping, and followed her to Zenosha, only to be attacked by the Brood. Terra-X was later resurrected by Brother Brood, completely under the control of the Brood and loyal to its cult. Although sent to attack the X-Patrol as a whole, her main target was Beastling, her former love-interest. She mocked Jericho, calling him "her replacement", and was about to kill him when Elasti-Girl flew into her ear-canal and put Terra-X out of action.
abilities: Terra-X is also very skilled in the use of her long-handled axe.

terraformer force of nature.name: Terraformer (Force of Nature)
terraformer force of nature.origin: ===Origin=== According to Omar Barrenos, Terraformer was a vegetable being called a Simuloid that was given sentience and human form by Plantman. Terraformer was recruited by Project: Earth to be part of their strike force, the Force of Nature, although the details of his recruitment and how the Project first learned of him remain a mystery. Terraformer participated in the Force of Nature's first public mission, against developers in the Amazon Jungle, which brought the team into conflict with the New Warriors. During the battle, he was struck by a microwave blast from Firestar and was dehydrated, reducing him to an inanimate plant form. Over time, Terraformer returned to a humanoid shape but never regained his facade of humanity. He was never seen during a Force of Nature mission overseas in Trans-Sabal. ===Imprisoned into the Vault=== The Force of Nature was incarcerated at the Vault prison, alongside Wizard and Gargantua. Terraformer's need for symbiotic contact with plant life reduced him to the point of insanity, and he instigated several riots among the prisoners. Fellow prisoner Vance Astrovik brought him a potted plant from the warden's office as a demonstration that the prisoners should be treated compassionately. ===Dark Reign=== thumb|275px|left|Terraformer met his death He later joined the Initiative, when the Force of Nature was made the team of Oregon. He participated to the sanction-offensive of the Initiative against the seceding Heavy Hitters and later to the H.A.M.M.E.R. assault on Asgard, and was seemingly killed by Heimdall.
powers: he can manipulate them, but he also needs to maintain contact with them for his own mental health, and perhaps his physical existence.

terrana.name: Terrana
terrana.origin: Terrana was a Dark Elf was chosen by Malekith to help him hunt down Iron Man, who had arrived to Svartalfheim in order to retrieve the rings of the Mandarin the villain had taken, for which the Accursed gave her the Spectral Ring. She was given a special secret mission by Malekith. Upon returning to Svartalfheim after fulfilling her mission, Terrana was attacked by the other Mandarins, but managed to escape. When she encountered Malekith, who had just fleed from being almost killed by Iron Man, she tried to tell him that the other Mandarins were on his trail, but before she could say anything, the other Mandarins arrived and attacked Malekith. The secret mission was later revealed to have been the extraction of the Bride's offspring from her body, for Malekith to raise it as his heir.

terrance hoffman.species: Human, formerly artificial mutant powered by the energies of Fatale, Abyss, and Reaper
terrance hoffman.origin: thumb|left|Dr. Terrance Hoffman ===Origin=== Dr. Terrance Hoffman was a scientist of A.I.M. who was looking for mutants to achieve his goals. He spent his whole adult life looking to grant himself with mutant powers. ===Saving Fatale, Reaper, and Abyss=== Finding Fatale, Reaper, and Abyss frozen within the latters' Brimstone Dimension, he saved them from it only to capture them and drain their mutant energies. As he was about to dissect Fatale, drained as much as possible, his compound was attacked by Serval Industries' X-Factor, led by Polaris. thumb|left|The powering process ===Mutant=== Draining both Reaper and Abyss and overpowering himself, Hoffman gained giant size and energy manipulation, and killed the operator as he before he could stop the process, and then battled X-Factor. He was quickly defeated by Gambit and Quicksilver, the latter quickly transporting the former to his rear to deliver an explosive card, defeating Hoffman and seemingly depowering him, as he wasn't able to retain the energies while unconscious. Reaper tried to execute him while he was knocked out, under the protests of Polaris and the support of Fatale, but was denied the opportunity by Quicksilver, leading to an attempt to fight with the speedster, not over Hoffman's life but due to Pietro's involvement in the prisoner's fate. ===Recruited by Serval Industries=== Hoffman was left in the custody of X-Factor and send to Serval's head office, restrained, and tested to be still a human. There, Serval President Harrison Snow offered him a place in his company.
powers: thumb|right|Powered form Using the energies of Fatale, Abyss, and Reaper, Hoffman gained the following mutant powers: Giant Size: It is unknown if he had control over that power.

terrance sorenson.name: Terrance Sorenson
terrance sorenson.origin: ===Origin=== Terrance "Terry" Sorenson was the son of two well-achieved research scientists. Though his mother Margay was successful, his father David was widely disregarded due to his wild theories on altering thermodynamics. His father became frustrated and started drinking and abusing his wife and son. Eventually Terry, who was seventeen at the time, and his mom tried to leave David. While they were leaving, one of David Sorenson's experimental devices caused an explosion which killed him and mutated his son who had tried to save him. Terry's mother tried to cure her son's induced mutation, but he eventually mutated further and not only became more powerful but also mentally unstable. Terry turned to crime after his mother used up their money with her experiments, taking on the name "Equinox." After a brief fight with Spider-Man, Equinox went up against Human Torch and Iceman, but managed to escape. He again fought against Spider-Man, who teamed up with Wasp, Yellowjacket, and Margay Sorenson by negating his powers with a thermic stabilizer that had been built in the Fantastic Four's lab. Terry was later seen able to control his powers after serving as a test subject at Project: PEGASUS and joining a support group for former criminals called Vil-Anon. He renounced crime and started a family, though his wife died and his daughter Janet inherited his powers, unintentionally causing several fires. Terry became frustrated trying to teach his daughter to control her powers, and became physically violent with her. Suspecting that Terry was hurting his daughter and that he had caused the fires, Sam Wilson, a.k.a. Falcon, intervened and had a quick skirmish with Equinox. After learning the truth of the situation, Falcon appeared on Terry's behalf in court, and Terry was able to go free. Afterwards Falcon also helped the Sorensons contact someone who could help Janet control her powers and help Terry overcome his abusive tendencies. ===Civil War=== Terry joined a group of super-villains during the first superhuman Civil War, preferring to leave the country with them, but was arrested by the Heroes for Hire and incarcerated in the Negative Zone Prison 42 where he remained after the breakout enacted by Captain America's forces. ===Freedom Force=== Equinox joined Freedom Force, the Montana Initiative, and was kidnapped by the Skrulls and a Skrull replacement who took his place. This imposter was killed during the Secret Invasion. Equinox re-joined the team and, under Osborn's administration, participated in the sanctioned attack of the Initiative against the seceding Heavy Hitters. ===Back to Criminality=== With the dissolution of Osborne's Initiative, Terry wreaked havoc in East Harlem, hoping to extort money out of people by torching buildings, demanding protection money, and threatening responding firefighters. To stop him, Spider-Man produced bombs filled with thermoreactive foam which quickly contained him. After the Avengers vs. X-Men conflict, a riot started at Terry's prison, and the only heroes able to respond were Rogue and Mimic. Quickly outnumbered, it was proposed by Armadillo, Man-Bull, and Equinox that the heroes borrow their powers in order to defeat their fellow inmates. Terry explained to Rogue that he wanted to repent so he might get out of jail sooner to take care of his daughter. ===Honor the Dynasty=== Equinox was later part of a Mr. Gryphon's plan. Gryphon was secretly an alternate Kang the Conqueror, so he used his time-powers to summon a lot of "Equinoxes" from some futures where Gryphon have won in order to fight the Avengers. The various Equinoxes were winning, before Spider-Man decided to pretend to betray the Avengers, all of the Equinoxes were not surprised of that...except for one of them: the present Equinox, who was at that point knocked out by Spider-Man; this event changed the future, so the other Equinoxes disappeared.

Gryphon was secretly an alternate Kang the Conqueror, so he used his time-powers to summon a lot of "Equinoxes" from some futures where Gryphon have won in order to fight the Avengers. The various Equinoxes were winning, before Spider-Man decided to pretend to betray the Avengers, all of the Equinoxes were not surprised of that...except for one of them: the present Equinox, who was at that point knocked out by Spider-Man; this event changed the future, so the other Equinoxes disappeared.

terrex.name: Terrex
terrex.origin: Terrex is a creation of the Eternals of Titan. Terrex was utilized to help Kerwin J. Broderick gain control of San Francisco. Moondragon mistakenly thought San Francisco was under the influence of Thanos and assisted Broderick with her powers and alien technology. Later, the aging Broderick melded his body and essence and merged with Terrex, with Broderick's psyche powering the being. Terrex was the embodiment of the Life Force. He claimed to have total power over any life form, both plant or human. As a demonstration, he drained the life force of a San Francisco policeman, killing him. Terrex was destroyed by the combined efforts of Moondragon, Angar the Screamer, Captain Marvel, Daredevil, and the Black Widow.

terri cooper.name: Terri Cooper
terri cooper.origin: Terri Cooper was a classmate of Robbie Baldwin's who at the time was operating as the Masked Marvel, later Speedball. Terri, like the rest of her classmates, was unaware of Robbie's double life. Unbeknownst to Terri, Robbie had a crush on her, but only saw him as a casual friend. She even accepted David Beals' prom proposal due to Robbie being sick at the time. However, she did have a crush on the Masked Marvel persona and managed to see him in action. She openly described the Masked Marvel as "hotter than Mel Gibson and Corey Haim rolled into one", despite the fact that she was incapable of seeing his face. She was on a field trip with Robbie and Dave when she witnessed Jolly Roger make off with a pirate exhibit's treasure. She joined with Dave and Doris to explore Springdale's coastal shore, but they were grossed out and decided to head to the mall instead, unaware that Robbie as the Masked Marvel was facing Jolly Roger. She regretted leaving with Dave as the next day as Robbie was hailed a hero for "finding" a flintlock pistol which Terri found amusing.

terrible old man.name: Terrible Old Man
terrible old man.origin: A strange old man, "so old that no one can remember when he was young, and so taciturn that few know his real name," lives alone in an ancient house on Water St. in the town of Kingsport . Few know the details of the old man's life, but it is believed that he once captained East Indian clipper ships in his youth and accumulated great riches throughout his life. Those who had visited the property had seen bizarre collections of stones in the front yard and observed the old man carrying on conversations with mysterious bottles on his table, which make "certain definite vibrations as if in answer." Most locals take care to avoid the man and his house.

terrigene.name: Terrigene
terrigene.species: Human enhanced by the use of Terrigen-mutated Inhuman DNA
terrigene.origin: Raised by a pair of geneticists who were tenured at a small mid-western university campus, she was very proud of her parents and went on to become a geneticist herself. Her research led her to study and encourage genetic mutations, and she held an affinity for those individuals who were set apart from others. However, her work was censured and banned, and her embarrassed family estranged themselves from her. Feeling lonely without family or career she sought to create a new family. Somehow establishing a high-tech base in the Andes Mountains, she hired the mercenary known as the Janissary to capture one of the members of the race of Inhumans, that she might duplicate and synthesize their mutagenic Terrigen, with which she could empower herself and others, forming another family. The Janissary brought her Sporr, and she successfully isolated the Terrigen, using it to mutate herself, taking the new name Terrigene. She was confronted by Crystal, who had been summoned by Sporr, and who managed to overpower her. Crystal used flames against Terrigene, and the flames hastened the process of her body proving insufficient to contain the terrigenated DNA. The defeated Terrigene explained her goal to Crystal, then convinced the Inhuman to take Sporr and leave her behind, so that her body might shake off the damage she had inflicted on herself.
powers: Terrigene can fly and project energy blasts. She may have had additional powers, though she did not demonstrate them.
abilities: She was highly skilled in the field of genetics.

terror shreck.name: Terror (Shreck)
terror shreck.origin: ===Origin=== At some point in the distant past, a tribe of early humans hunted and fought a demon that had been preying upon them. The demon resembled a green bear, with a series of long, thin spikes protruding from its face and along its spine. The man who killed the bear was cursed by victory to assume the demon's form - his skin took on its green, decaying form, and the spikes from its face appeared on his. He gained the beast's ability to merge the limbs of others with his own body, but was shunned by the tribe he had helped to protect. Over the years, he adopted names that reflected people's reaction to him, and by the Dark Ages he had adapted the Germanic "schreck" (scare, fright) as his name. ===Shreck=== At that point looking mostly human, Shreck was the squire to a powerful Shadow who was then calling himself Draghignazzo. Gravely injured in battle, Draghignazzo had Shreck bury him to create the illusion that he was actually dead, so he could heal in peace - a process that would take centuries. In the meantime, Shreck became a full knight, fighting side-by-side with Talita, a woman he loved and who, remarkably, loved him back. She soon died, however, and Shreck had her left hand encased in metal and hermetically sealed so that he might remember her touch forever, the one part of his amalgamated body that would never decay. Shreck's activities from that time until the mid-1980s are unknown, but when he was next seen, he had been serving for several years as the enforcer for the Ravenscore crime family. During an argument, Eric Ravenscore blasted off one of Ripley Weaver's metal hands, which Shreck quietly collected for later use. In Turkey, Shreck was found by two drug dealers who had been in a confrontation with the heroic Michael Devlin, knight in the Order of St. George. Taking one of the dealers' eyes for his own, Shreck recognized Devlin, and sought to prevent him from leaving Turkey. He crashed a plane on the runway at the Turkish airport, forcing Devlin to leave via train. The two fought and, with help from his traveling companions, Devlin won. Shreck's legs were chained to one car of the train, which was then uncoupled. Determined to follow Devlin, he grabbed the rail of the next car forward, but the mass and momentum of the separating cars eventually tore his legs off. Shreck survived, of course, but now held a personal grudge against Devlin, rather than the cold, impersonal "just business" attitude he displayed toward most of his victims. Shreck informed the Ravenscores that he would be leaving their employ temporarily, until he had taken his revenge on Devlin. By this time, Draghignazzo had returned and was posing as the hero Dr. Zero. Shreck sought Zero's permission to kill Devlin, but was denied; he could stalk Devlin, but only kill him if he told Zero first. Tracking Devlin to Nicaragua, Shreck managed to get the best of him after a protected brawl, then proceeded to crucify the man to a tree - he didn't have permission to kill Devlin, but he could certainly let him die. Devlin freed himself, however, and ambushed Shreck, continuing their fight. The pair tumbled over a waterfall, but the battle was only decided when Devlin dumped Shreck in a lake that was teeming with piranhas. He offered Shreck his hand, but when it became obvious the killer was taking that literally, he let go, and Shreck sank to the bottom. thumb|left|Appearance when he reached Earth-616 Hours later, after the fish had departed, scavengers found Shreck's skeleton and prepared to remove the gold fillings in his teeth. Despite the massive damage he'd incurred, Shreck was still alive, and rebuilt his body from the men who had found him. It was some time after this that Shreck journeyed through unknown means to Earth-616 and set himself up as the mercenary assassin Terror. He had an unspecified history with Wolverine, a "long-standing series of markers" between them. Terror first appeared in the "modern" Marvel universe when he was contacted by Las Vegas mobster Deragon, looking for an advantage in the process of dividing the Kingpin's criminal empire. While in Las Vegas, he met Daredevil, and offered him information in exchange for helping to protect him from New York City's many superhumans, should the need arise. He next assisted Wolverine and Jubilee against a group of murderous eco-saboteurs. Hired to perform a hit on crime lord Piranha Jones, Terror found himself at odds with the Punisher, who also wanted Jones dead. Getting in each other's way, the two lost Jones as they fought among themselves. ===Mercs for Money=== When Deadpool founded the Mercs for Money, he employed the services of Terror, among numerous other mercenaries, to pose as him in order to extend his reach across the globe. In one of his missions, Terror patrolled the streets of New York along with fellow teammate Foolkiller. The Mercs for Money eventually became disgruntled by Deadpool, from the way he treated them to the delays in their paychecks

weaknesses: His body is in a constant state of decay, requiring him to constantly replace all parts of his body.

terry burns.name: Terry Burns
terry burns.origin: Terry Burns was a worker at Brandywine Pharmaceutical Company in New York City, but he was fired. He was approached by supervillain Abner Jenkins, the Beetle, who had been partially released from jail and was pretending to have reformed. The Beetle hired Burns and other common thugs who were impressed at Jenkins' past. Burns simultaneously attended to demonstration due to Brandywine workers being on strike, and he even threw a can to the police - which led to Spider-man visibly harassing Burns in public, as he had taken Burns for a dangerous criminal. The Bettle sent Burns to steal drugs at Brandywine to fund the gang's criminal operations. In the night, dressed in black and wearing a ski mask, Burns left the building, but was found by Spider-man again. Seeing that capture was highly likely, Burns swallowed the stolen drugs so the loot wouldn't be found on him. While Burns complained to Spider-man that Brandywine was destroying jobs, Spider-man entangled Burns in his web fluid (which was to melt in one hour), then notified the security guard (so that Burns would be watched when the fluid melted). Yet the Beetle was keepign an eye on Burns and had seen the event, so he knocked down the guard to recover Burns and the drugs. Then the Beetle, who has notable mechanic skills, decided to use the available web fluid to duplicate it. He took Burns and the fluid to his lair - but Burns died suddenly because of a drug overdose (which the Beetle took for a heart attack due to Burns fear to the Beetle's imposing presence). He was approached by supervillain Abner Jenkins, the Beetle, who had been partially released from jail and was pretending to have reformed. The Beetle hired Burns and other common thugs who were impressed at Jenkins' past. Burns simultaneously attended to demonstration due to Brandywine workers being on strike, and he even threw a can to the police - which led to Spider-man visibly harassing Burns in public, as he had taken Burns for a dangerous criminal. The Bettle sent Burns to steal drugs at Brandywine to fund the gang's criminal operations. In the night, dressed in black and wearing a ski mask, Burns left the building, but was found by Spider-man again. Seeing that capture was highly likely, Burns swallowed the stolen drugs so the loot wouldn't be found on him. While Burns complained to Spider-man that Brandywine was destroying jobs, Spider-man entangled Burns in his web fluid (which was to melt in one hour), then notified the security guard (so that Burns would be watched when the fluid melted). terry raymond.name: Terry Raymond
terry raymond.origin: After his mutant powers manifested, Terry felt like an outsider and even wanted to die. He was found by Professor X, who brought the orphan to the Xavier Institute, where Terry joined the X-Men as T-Ray. T-Ray and the rest of the X-Men fought a Sentinel, and after T-Ray blasted it with his mutant powers, it almost fell on him before he was teleported to safety by Nightcrawler. After they returned to the Institute, Professor X lectured T-Ray. Intent on proving himself, T-Ray sneaked into the Danger Room late at night and started a training session. However, it went awry and some equipment blew up, burning Terry's face. He was taken to the med-lab. After recovering, T-Ray spent the next month as a reclusive in his room, upset over his facial deformities (his powers also no longer worked properly due to psychological blocks). Nightcrawler tried to give him advice, but Terry asked to be left alone. He left the Institute the following day and returned to Queens, where he went back to high school. He tried his best to keep his scars covered, but a teacher, not realizing Terry's injuries, had him remove his cap and glasses in the classroom, to the horror of his fellow students. As he later tried to ignore fellow schoolmates mocking him, he was telepathically contacted by Professor X. He told Xavier to leave him alone. A girl at school named Sylvia became interested in him and sat with him at lunch, asking about how he got his scars. He also made friends with a boy named Gary. While practicing basketball, Terry was approached by Magneto to join his Brotherhood of Mutants. Terry declined, and Magneto went to attack him for doing so, but the X-Men arrived, having wanted to check on the boy, and engaged Magneto in battle. Magneto easily handled the mutants until T-Ray stepped in and blasted him; his powers having returned. Unable to handle the combined attack, Magneto fled. T-Ray was welcomed back into the X-Men, and they rushed off to save a young mutant in Kansas from Sentinels. He was one of the students at the Xavier Institute that was depowered due to M-Day and most likely killed when the bus exploded.
powers: T-Ray's powers create vibrations that often cause earthquake and avalanche-like effects.

terry schreck.name: Terry Schreck
terry schreck.origin: Terry Schreck was a detective for the NYPD who was following the trail of a criminal named Stone along with his partners Brigid O'Reilly and Vernon Brooks. When they raided Stone's house, which Stone had shorlty before abandonded, they discovered it was one of the numerous ex-Roxxon labs in the city. thumb|left|Prior to transformation After pinning down Stone in an alleyway, the detectives discovered him and his partner Styx fighting the Young Ultimates. Terry was disfigured and fatally injured when Styx touched him, and O'Reilly, Vernon, and the Ultimates were soon surrounded by the Serpent Skulls. The NYPD detectives and the Ultimates confronted the Skulls until the arrival of a SWAT team caused both the group of heroes and the group of villains to flee. Terry was taken to Roosevelt Hospital where he died hours later. While his body was being prepared for autopsy, it disappeared, leaving a trace of footprints behind. Terry had survived, and was roaming through West Side Highway until a truck hit him and made him fall through an open manhole to the sewer.

terry vance.name: Terry Vance
terry vance.origin: Terry Vance was a brilliant teenage detective who was active during the 1940s. He frequently solved crimes along with his pet monkey Dr. Watson and his best friend, reporter Deadline Dawson. During the chronicles of his career between the years 1940 to 1944, he became a respected individual among local law enforcement as well as the FBI and military intelligence thanks to his constant thwarting of criminals and Axis spies during the course of World War II. ===1940=== In his first recorded adventure, Terry Vance offered his aid in learning who had shot and killed a local doctor. Although turned away by the police, Terry's detective skills found a hidden gun that was rigged to fire when a timer was triggered. Terry soon pieced together the clues to the murder to determine that the killer was the doctor's step-son who wished to cash in on the family wealth before an official will could be drawn up. Terry assisted in the capture of the step-son and turned him over to the authorities. When witnessing a wreck during an auto race, Terry discovered mercury at the crash site and followed some suspicious men who had mercury in their possession. He followed them back to their hideout and learned that they were using a man called the "Master Mechanic" to place mercury in the tires of car they wished to lose the races so that they could hedge bets into their favor. Although Terry was discovered and tied up by the crooks, he was saved by Deadline Dawson, and the pair alerted the authorities, leading to the crooks' capture. Next, while out for a joy ride, Terry and Deadline got caught in a rainstorm and sought cover at a nearby mansion. There, they helped protect a businessman from being murdered by his greedy partner. Later, Terry uncovered a plot to steal valuable paintings from the local art museum and were replaced with phonies. Following that adventure, Terry witnessed the kidnapping of actress Diana Dunn and helped rescue her and thwart her captors. ===1941=== Accompanying Deadline Dawson to cover a human interest story regarding the living conditions in the city's slums, the pair discovered the body of a murdered writer. Terry soon deduced that the writer was killed by his own son who used poisoned candles to kill his father so that he could cash in on the story he was working on. While on a fishing trip with reporter Scoop O'Brien, Terry and Deadline discovered the abandoned yacht owned by Fred Rochelle. They soon pieced together clues to find that Rochelle was murdered by Pinelli, the owner of the Swan Club over his illegal gambling debts. Terry soon came to the aid of a man named Burk who was accused of a series of bombings, including that of his employer the Broome Chemical Plant. However, Terry soon deduced that the real culprit was Killer D'Arcy and his gang who had framed Burk for the explosions. Active in his school, Terry convinced the principal to allow them to have a bike club to further their education. When the principal refused to provide the students with a bike rack to lock up their bikes, they were stolen, repainted, and sold to other children. Terry investigated the situation and determined that the school janitor was behind the theft of the bikes. His discovery convinced the principal that bike racks were necessary and was nominated president of the bike club. Out with his bike club, Terry and the others got caught in the rain and sought shelter in a nearby mansion that was reported to be haunted. Inside they stumbled upon a meeting between local mobster and Mr. Grabbit, a city official. Using their cover, Terry and the others spooked Grabbit into ceasing his shady dealings with the mobster and got the crook arrested. Investigating the scene of a bank robbery, Terry discovered that the crooks learned the combination of the bank's safe thanks to a radio unit that recorded the sound of the safe tumblers. Although Inspector Crane was killed for his refusal to drop the case, Terry learned the killers' identities and brought them to justice. Later, having developed a remote control plane (which he used to rescue a pair of girls who had fallen through ice), Terry was invited to Washington, D.C. to present it to the military for its possible use in the war effort. When foreign spies attempted to sabotage an aircraft carrying a military official interested in seeing the plane, Terry saved them by using his plane to act as makeshift landing gear. Later, when the spies attempted to steal the plane, Terry used his remote control to call the plane back, causing the spies to crash their truck, killing them. Terry's invention was then accepted by the military. Returning home, Terry next investigated a series of "phantom robberies" that involved the theft of highly inaccessible valuables. Terry's trail led him to a local circus where he uncovered that the monkey trainer had used his monkeys to rob the various locations. terry wilke.name: Terry Wilke
terry wilke.origin: thumb|left|200px|Terry Wilke After the incident known as the White Event, Wilke developed paranormal powers, in his case the ability to project concussive force. He subsequently became a patient at the Clinic for Paranormal Research in Wisconsin. Wilke seemed to be one of the more low-profile patients, not joining any of the special interest groups that sprang up among the patients. When the police raided the Clinic to investigate the deaths of some staff members that had been covered up, Wilke was in the middle of a physical therapy session at the Clinic's pool with physical therapist Juris Ziegler. When the police entered the pool area, guns drawn, Ziegler warned Wilke not to resist, but he hit one of the cops with a concussive blast anyway and he and Ziegler were both shot – Ziegler in the back and Wilke at the side of his stomach. It is unknown if he survived this injury. If he did, it is probable that like other adult male paranormals, he would have been drafted into the army.
powers: Wilke could project concussive force as blasts. When these blasts struck certain substances, they would burst into flame.

terry wright.name: Terry Wright
terry wright.origin: Terry Wright was an Army veteran who ran a veterans center in Las Vegas. Shortly after Kaine Parker moved to Las Vegas, Terry came across him at the Rockerz cafe. Thinking that his scarred face could've been caused by an army incident, she offered him to visit her shelter. Following Hydra's ravaging of the city, the owner of the building rented by the center saw himself forced to sell the property since it was intact to help repair those severely damaged. Kaine decided to take advantage of his fellow clone's Ben Reilly connection to casino-owner Cassandra Mercury to help the shelter since they had little to no money. After helping rescue Cassandra from kidnapping as the Scarlet Spider, Kaine told her the story of Terry's center. She decided to help them out, and issued a cheque which got them out of their financial trouble.

tesi lexico.name: Tesi Lexico
tesi lexico.origin: Tesi Lexico was the daughter of Professor Regean Lexico who learned of the powerful energy source he dubbed "Star Dust" that he learned was located on the so-called star named Cygni. Knowing that it was a powerful replacement for radium, he stowed away on the rocket owned by Zephyr Jones, and Tesi snuck onboard behind him. Her father helf Zephyr and his pal Corky Grogan at gunpoint Tesi managed to convince the pair to take them there. On the "star", Lexico sprayed both Zephyr and Corky with a chemical that would allow them to survive on the surface. Lexico and Tesi were soon captured by the dwarfish Cygnians and needed to be rescued by Zephyr and Corky. After their attackers were buried under tons of rock, they collected 50 pounds of "Star Dust" and left for a return trip from Earth.

tesla tarasova.name: Tesla Tarasova
tesla tarasova.origin: Born to Linus Tarasov - a KGB scientist and an unnamed mother, Tesla didn't have a terrific start in life, as her mother died in childbirth and her father wanted out. Doing so, he took Tesla away - raising her in a remote, isolated area in Russia. When she was six (?) Linus was shot in front of her by James "Bucky" Barnes, the Winter Soldier. Taking her back to the KGB, she was forced to listen to George Michael's "Wake Me Up" on the stereo every day while staring at the word "Life" written across a chalkboard as if it had some significant meaning. Tesla took one thing with her to this Orphanage and that was her father's books The Lion and The Shepherd. This book told Tesla all she needed for something in her future. When she turned 11, Tesla let her rough exterior down for a possible friend only to be quickly betrayed. It was then that Tesla learned there is no one but herself to depend on. From that day on she was "The Electric Ghost". This book is more than just a book it teaches Tesla how to bend and shape the Cosmic to her pattern, the way she wants. Effectively giving her the power to make and create anything she want, this again comes later. As time went on at the school things got worse she began to turn in on herself, letting any fragments go of the young girl that was once there. Eventually, she was sold as a child soldier to a man who became her lover. One day, she killed him and struck out on her own, attacking S.H.I.E.L.D. installations, drawing the attention of Nick Fury who pointed Bucky at her. With the help of Agent Joe Robards, he tracked her down and confronted her, trying to talk her down from her stated intention of rewriting history.

tess walker.name: Tess Walker
tess walker.origin: Tess is the daughter of Chance Walker. She sometimes brought food to her father and other loggers in her community. She was particularly interested when her father arrested and incarcerated Prince Namor. Namor had brainwashed at the time by Master Khan at the time and did not know his true identity. Claiming to be bored with a lack of events in the town, Tess appeared to befriend Namor and offered to let him stay with her. Namor did so and became attracted to Tess. She soon revealed to him that she was part of an Eco-Terrorist group convinced him to aid her eco-terrorist group that was opposed to the loggers who were ravaging their countryside. Tess was also mysteriously allied with another group that was paying her money on the side. Namor joined with the eco-terrorists and attacked the loggers' camp at night. Suddenly, and individual with a large harvesting machine emerged killing both loggers and eco-terrorists alike. Upon investigation, Namor found out it was his "friend" Tess who had betrayed him.

tessa foswell.name: Tessa Foswell
tessa foswell.origin: Tessa Foswell was the wife of Frederick Foswell, a Daily Bugle reporter who turned to a life of crime as the Big Man and it cost him his life. When her son Freddie took up the mantle of Big Man to avenge his father, he kidnapped Foswell's boss J. Jonah Jameson, and whom he believed to be culprit, Spider-Man. Freddie used a series of holograms that retold Jameson's life to entice him into joining his side, one of them being a hologram of Tessa at Foswell's funeral which reminded Jonah of his promise to make Spider-Man pay for her husband's death.

tessa goodwin.name: Tessa Goodwin
tessa goodwin.origin: Tessa was in New York City where she came upon gang members recently released from Cloak's cloak. Bashing their heads in, she then drank their blood and turned into a bat, heading off in search of Cloak, whose power she sought. In Central Park, she ran into Cloak and his partner Dagger, who were on patrol. Claiming to have been attacked by "some...thing" she sought their protection. Leading the pair into a church, she caused Dagger to fall into a trap, but Dagger escaped just as she was preparing to feast on Cloak. Quickly dispatching Dagger, Tessa hypnotized Cloak into unleashing his power, seeking to control him. As Cloak unleashed his power, she realized that he was too powerful to control, and the darkness that emanated from his cloak threatened to overwhelm her, but Dagger leaped to her rescue, convincing Cloak to leave Tessa alone. Angry over being used, Cloak threatened to absorb her into his cloak anyway, but was stopped by Dagger, who told him that he was better than that.
powers: Tessa had the conventional abilities of a vampire, including , the ability to turn into a bat, the ability to gather darkness around her

tetra.name: Tetra
tetra.species: Human possessed by a demon, giving her magic powers (Magician)
tetra.origin: Tetra was one of the many daughters of the Brythunian nobleman Zacharus. When she was seventeen, Zacharus took Tetra with him on a quest in the Pictish Wilderness to find the half of a treasure map, the other half being sewn into Tetra's dress. When their caravan was attacked by Picts, Zacharus was captured. Conan rescued Tetra, then reunited father and daughter, though Zacharus did abandon Tetra in the village. Conan was forced to battle the entire village, and was only saved by Tetra who grabbed and threatened to stab the shaman Kawagne. The trio then fled in search of the map. Tetra was possessed by the power of the ancient sorcerer Nostume. She she was caught by the Demon Wolf, she was doomed to wander the time stream for all eternity, cursed with everlasting life and near-limitless eldritch power, embodying the undying force of an ageless evil. She then journeyed back through the time stream to kill Conan, when he was a kid in Cimmeria, but she eventually reconsidered and left. She was later killed by Conan to prevent the demon from taking control and hurting people.
abilities: Tetra was a skilled fighter in unarmed and armed combat after being trained by Conan, easily killing ten men who harassed her. She was skilled in the use of weapons like swords, clubs, and a bow. She was also skilled in horseback riding.
weapons: Swords, clubs, a bow and arrows
weaknesses: She can still be injured and even killed. She formerly had trouble controlling the power she possessed.
